source.title: Learning to grok: Emergence of in-context learning and skill composition in modular arithmetic tasks
source.authors: Tianyu He; Darshil Doshi; Aritra Das; Andrey Gromov

record.tranche_reason: Extends modular-arithmetic generalization research to in-context learning over a family of tasks, and reports training and out-of-distribution performance outcomes relevant to V1. It is not a direct test of the original single-task grokking setup.
record.gate_note: The study measures in-context performance on unseen task vectors while varying pre-training task diversity and, in some experiments, optimization steps. It does not test the classic setting of perfect training accuracy followed by a late test-accuracy rise as the number of training examples shrinks. Its interpretability analyses do not track circuit formation over optimization or test continuous progress measures.
record.test_reason: The study trains transformers on a family of in-context modular arithmetic tasks. It maps end-of-training (early-stopped) accuracy against task diversity (n_i.d.) and the fraction of inputs seen (α). No result measures a test-accuracy jump occurring long after training accuracy saturates, or how such a delay scales with training-set size. The grokking link is by analogy only: the authors say the α-driven rise in in-distribution generalization is 'in correspondence with' grokking. The transient o.o.d. accuracy is in-context generalization rising and then falling with continued training. That is a different construct from V1's delayed generalization, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors find that increasing pre-training task diversity shifts GPT-style models from in-distribution memorization or generalization to out-of-distribution in-context generalization. At least two blocks are needed for this. For deeper models the o.o.d. phase is transient and needs early stopping. Generalizing models have structured circle-of-circles representations. The d=4 model shifts from Ratio Matching to Modular Regression as shots increase, while the d=2 model stays with Ratio Matching.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains GPT-style models on a family of linear modular functions and evaluates in-context generalization to unseen task vectors. The original grokking setup concerns training and test examples for a task, rather than this task-family ICL setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Out-of-distribution generalization depends on pre-training task diversity and model depth; for the d = 6 model at ni.d. = 2^8 it is transient over training. The paper also reports that larger p requires more pre-training tasks to generalize.

fits_no_version.finding: For d=6 at n_i.d.=2^8, o.o.d. in-context accuracy rises and then decays with continued training. The authors attribute this to memorizing circuits eventually prevailing over generalizing ones. For d=4, ICL is also transient at lower α or n_i.d.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In multi-task in-context modular arithmetic, out-of-distribution generalization can be transient, the reverse of grokking's ordering, depending on task diversity and model capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: o.o.d. in-context generalization emerges only above a threshold number of pre-training tasks (n_i.d. ≥ 256 for d=6, p=29). Pre-training accuracy falls as o.o.d. accuracy rises.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task diversity drives a memorization-to-generalization transition for in-context learning of modular functions, with a memorization–generalization trade-off.

record.peer_reviewed: 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)
record.problems: The tested setup is an algorithmic in-context-learning task family rather than the classic single-task grokking setup. The text does not provide exact accuracy values for the relevant curves, and the main phase diagrams use early stopping and select the best result from three random seeds. The optimization curves are averaged over three seeds with standard error labeled, but exact errors are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: Delayed test-accuracy jump after training saturation, and delay growing as the training set shrinks. Neither is measured.
No tracking of circuit formation or progress measures over training.
No non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
Weight decay is fixed at 2.0. There is no critical-dataset-size or ungrokking test.
Different depths use different algorithms (Ratio Matching vs Modular Regression), but this is not framed or tested as a run-to-run convergence question.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/'tests' classification overstates the link. Grokking is cited as inspiration and analogy, but no result measures delayed generalization after training saturation. Phase diagrams use early stopping and the best of 3 seeds. Curve values are not given numerically in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies the number of pre-training task vectors, not training-set size for a single task. It does not establish that training accuracy reaches perfect saturation before a near-perfect test jump, or that the delay grows as the training set shrinks.

The study identifies algorithms and circuit-like structures in trained models, but does not track their gradual formation and removal over training or test whether continuous progress measures anticipate an accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition test.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
Weight decay is used in training, but the efficiency account, critical dataset size, and ungrokking prediction are not tested.
The study does not test whether different runs converge to the same algorithm across architectures and hyperparameters.
No adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point softmax artifact challenge is tested.

rows.subject: d = 6 model
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of pre-training task vectors and measured accuracy on the out-of-distribution test set.
rows.value: The model generalizes to new tasks when ni.d. ≥ 256; the phase diagram uses a 75% threshold to define phases.
rows.note: This is a transition across task diversity, not a reported late test-accuracy jump after perfect training accuracy.
rows.check: This is a transition across the number of pre-training tasks in an early-stopped, best-of-3-seeds phase diagram. It is not accuracy over training time, so it cannot show V1's post-saturation delay.

rows.subject: d = 6 model
rows.operation_detail: Measured pre-training and out-of-distribution test performance during optimization.
rows.measure: Out-of-distribution test accuracy over training steps
rows.value: The out-of-distribution performance first improves and then degrades; the authors describe this generalization ability as transient.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error is labeled for the curves, but its values are not stated in the text.
rows.note: The text reports a non-monotonic trajectory, not a sustained rise to near-perfect accuracy after training accuracy saturates.
rows.check: o.o.d. in-context accuracy rises and then falls over training at n_i.d.=2^8. No delay after train saturation is reported. This is transient ICL, a different construct; see fits_no_version.

rows.subject: d = 6 model
rows.operation_detail: Compared pre-training performance with out-of-distribution performance in the task-diversity phase diagram.
rows.measure: Pre-training accuracy as out-of-distribution performance increases
rows.value: The authors report that pre-training performance simultaneously degrades as out-of-distribution performance increases.
rows.note: This reported trade-off differs from the version’s picture of training accuracy remaining saturated while test accuracy rises.
rows.check: Marked 'reversed', which is wrong. V1 makes no claim about pre-training accuracy across task diversity. The trade-off is a cross-condition comparison, not a time-course result.

rows.subject: d = 4 model
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of pre-training task vectors and measured out-of-distribution accuracy.
rows.value: Out-of-distribution generalization emerges only with a large enough number of pre-training tasks; performance degrades as model capacity decreases.
rows.note: The text does not specify a late-overfitting accuracy jump or a delay that grows as the training set shrinks.
rows.check: Early-stopped phase diagram across task diversity for d=4. It has no measure of delay.

rows.subject: d = 2 model
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of pre-training task vectors and measured out-of-distribution accuracy.
rows.value: Out-of-distribution generalization emerges only with a large enough number of pre-training tasks; the authors say this small model skips the in-distribution generalization phase and jumps from memorization to out-of-distribution generalization.
rows.note: The described jump is across generalization phases as task diversity changes, not a delayed test-accuracy jump over optimization after perfect training accuracy.
rows.check: The 'jump' for d=2 is across generalization phases as task diversity changes, not over optimization steps.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The tested modular in-context task setting across d = 2, d = 4, and d = 6 models
reader_labels.reason: Out-of-distribution generalization appears with sufficient task diversity, but the d = 6, ni.d. = 2^8 result is transient, and the study does not establish the classic post-saturation jump or a delay that increases as training examples shrink (R1–R5).
